svg.text: PDM audio over Gigabit Ethernet: signal flow and clocks, WAV file to 8 PDM microphones and back to the GUI

LP-AM243 Rev A, ICSSG0 + ICSSG1 at 333.33 MHz, PRU firmware only in the data path (the R5F configures and idles). Each column is one clock domain. Numbers: design.md, firmware headers, test_report.md (board run 2026-11-05).
WAV file or a capture set
each channel loops on its length
pings: RX IEP time to PRU0
so PRU1 wraps with an AND
real mics replace the source only
4 ms before a half is reused
AUDIO_OUT, to the last PC MAC
Clock and rate chain: one sample clock, the ICSSG0 core clock; everything else follows it

Who sets the time. PRU1 (ICSSG0) is the only free-running audio clock. RTU1 consumes the MSRAM ring at its rate and reports its position in every AUDIO_OUT status block; the PC pacer keeps 0.5 s ahead of that position, never of its own clock.

Alignment. Both directions carry sample indices. The PC places output by (HALF_SEQ - 1) x 64 + part x 32 and the GUI lines the IN and OUT panes up by index, so PC clock drift (+10.9 ppm measured) and network jitter never shift audio.

Measured (2026-11-05). Board audio latency 1.08 ms, constant (RTU1 takes a sample -> its AUDIO_OUT leaves the board, best case). 500 / 250 frames/s out / in, 0 lost, UNDERRUN and SD_OVF 0, GUI 60 fps, board PONG turnaround 0.3 to 32 us.
